evidence_detail: ATTACKS RUN, ALL FAILED TO OVERTURN 16.60. (1) TEMPERATURE-BUCKET ARTEFACT? NO. Measured dEps/dT = -0.1764/K (je3007666, 5 pts 288-308 K, R2=0.9988; je900503p gives -0.1520/K). The 4 observations sit at 298.00 and 298.15 K, a 0.15 K span, worth 0.0265 in eps = 2.6% of the 1.02 gap. Temperature explains 2.6%, not 'most'. The T=298 bucket is NOT the cause of the spread. The 17.60 value corrected to 298.15 K would be 17.574 - still far from 16.60. (2) DUPLICATE SOURCES? PARTLY. duplicate_observation_groups.csv records je3007666 and je800593p as byte-identical at 298.15 K (16.60/16.60). I verified this project-wide: across all 4 shared molecules and 15 shared (molecule,T) pairs, the two DOIs agree in 15/15 cases (100%). So 4 obs / 4 'sources' is really 3 distinct values. THE DEDUP DOES NOT MOVE THE ANSWER: median(17.60,16.58,16.60)=16.60, identical to the as-counted median. (3) IS 16.60 ARBITRARY? NO - THIS ATTACK FAILS. 16.60 is the median, it is the median under dedup too, and it coincides with the exact 298.15 K measurement (je3007666 = je800593p = 16.60 at 298.15 K). It is not the min (16.58 is) and not a lone pick. (4) COUNTER-EVIDENCE SEARCH: the real structure is 3 mutually-agreeing values (16.58, 16.60, 16.60; 16.58 vs 16.60 differ by 0.12%) versus ONE divergent value, 17.60 from 10.1016/j.fluid.2013.12.014. That leg is a PNA-N5227A network-analyzer measurement at 298.00 K carrying a stated expanded uncertainty of +/-1.90 = 10.8% of value, i.e. an interval of [15.70, 19.50] which CONTAINS 16.60. The three agreeing legs carry +/-0.06 (0.36%). The register flags this pair because build_source_conflict_register.py applies a flat REL_EPS_TOLERANCE=2% and never reads the stated uncertainties, so a 10.8% measurement is automatically 'in conflict' with 0.36% measurements. This is an artefact of the conflict detector's construction, not of temperature and not of a genuine source disagreement. (5) EXTERNAL CORROBORATION FOUND (searched, not assumed): data/raw/reaxys_w17g/observations.csv, an index independent of ThermoML, holds butan-2-ol eps=16.6 at T=298.14 K and eps=16.56 with no T, plus 16.72 at 298.15 K - all consistent with 16.60. The 17.6-17.8 region appears only at 288-293 K (17.51@293.15, 17.46@293.15, 18.47@288.15), which is exactly where dEps/dT says it should be. (6) NON-BLOCKING DEFECT (recorded, does not overturn the value): v06 does not actually aggregate a 298.15 K window. build_dataset_v06.py uses BAND_LOW/HIGH = 293.15/303.15 K, so the 16.6 is the median of a 10.0 K wide pool (3x17.51@293.15, 17.60@298.00, 16.58/16.60@298.15, 3x15.75@303.15, n=10) whose temperature label 298.15 K is the median of the pooled temperatures. The answer is right only because the pool happens to be near-symmetric about 298.15 K; a one-sided band gives 17.51 (293-298) or 16.165 (298-303). The label, not the value, is unsound. (7) LEDGER OMISSION: 3 pure butan-2-ol observations present in data/raw/thermoml_full/eps_observations.csv are absent from measurement_ledger_v1.csv ((298.2, 16.467), (308.2, 15.055), (318.2, 13.71)); the 298.2/16.467 point would further support 16.60. VERDICT: 16.60 is the median, dedup-robust, independently corroborated, and statistically indistinguishable from the only divergent leg under that leg's own stated uncertainty. Keep the value; fix the temperature label and make the conflict detector uncertainty-aware.

THE v06 VALUE 37.72 IS AN ARTEFACT OF DOUBLE-COUNTING ONE EXPERIMENT. THIS IS A FATAL, REPRODUCIBLE DEFECT. (1) DUPLICATE SOURCES - CONFIRMED AND DECISIVE. duplicate_observation_groups.csv records 10.1016/j.fluid.2008.01.024 and 10.1016/j.fluid.2009.07.009 as byte-identical at 303.15 K, both eps=37.72, both U=0.230. So '3 obs / 3 sources' is really 2 independent values: {37.72, 38.67}. (2) THE MEDIAN FLIPS ON DEDUP. As counted, median(37.72, 37.72, 38.67) = 37.72 = the v06 value. Deduped, median(37.72, 38.67) = 38.195, a shift of +0.475 (+1.26%). 37.72 is selected ONLY because one experiment is counted twice; with two genuine values there is no majority and 37.72 is the MINIMUM of the pair, not the median. The v06 'median_in_window' rule is therefore a coin-flip that happened to land on the low leg for a purely bookkeeping reason. (3) NOT A TEMPERATURE ARTEFACT. All three observations are at exactly 303.15 K (T span = 0.00 K); dEps/dT = -0.1376/K contributes 0.0% of the 2.52% gap. (4) THE DISAGREEMENT IS REAL, NOT NOISE. Unlike butan-2-ol, the stated uncertainties here are tight and the intervals do NOT overlap: 37.72 +/- 0.230 (0.61%) -> [37.490, 37.950] versus 38.67 +/- 0.387 (1.00%) -> [38.283, 39.057]. A gap of 0.80 with a union interval gap of 0.333 is a genuine inter-laboratory disagreement, not a low-precision outlier. The 2.52% spread also exceeds the project's own 2.00% relative tolerance. (5) MATERIAL OMISSION FROM THE LEDGER. data/raw/thermoml_full/eps_observations.csv contains 9 pure DMAc observations that never reach measurement_ledger_v1.csv: three at 293.15 K (39.653, 39.688, 39.695), three at 298.15 K (38.526, 38.586, 38.600) and three at 303.15 K (37.499, 37.515, 37.552). The three 303.15 K values (10.1016/j.jct.2017.11.011, U=+/-1.03) would change the 303.15 K population from {37.72, 37.72, 38.67} to include 37.499/37.515/37.552. The conflict was therefore adjudicated on an incomplete observation set - 22 raw rows exist, only 12 are in the ledger. (6) EXTERNAL SEARCH DOES NOT RESOLVE IT - IT WIDENS IT. data/raw/reaxys_w17g/observations.csv (independent of ThermoML) gives DMAc at 298.15 K: 37.79, 37.80, 37.80, 38.25, 38.60, and at 293.15 K: 38.30, 38.93, and 37.78/39.0 with no temperature, plus 42.5 and 43 at 308.14 K (evidently a different quantity or a gross outlier). The literature envelope at room temperature is roughly 37.4-38.9. BOTH 37.72 and 38.67 fall inside it, so neither can be declared canonical from the available evidence. data/raw/open_data_eps/eps_observations.csv adds 37.8 at 298.15 K (PMC8587213) - again inside the band, corroborating neither leg specifically. (7) THE RESIDUAL IS UNRESOLVABLE WITH IN-HOUSE EVIDENCE. Resolving 37.72 vs 38.67 requires the primary documents (sample purity/water content, method, calibration) for 10.1021/je9002515 (the parallel-plate high leg) and for the 37.72 leg. No such primary text is in the repository. VERDICT: HOLD. The v06 value is a duplicate-counting artefact, the disagreement is real and exceeds stated uncertainty, the observation set is incomplete, and no available evidence selects between the legs. Do not average. The row must not remain model_ready=true while this is unresolved.

SYSTEMIC FATAL FLAW: dataset_v06 does not consume measurement_conflict_register.csv at all. (1) SCALE OF THE LEAK. The register holds 56 conflicts, ALL of them resolution_status=UNRESOLVED. Mapping each register molecule_key against dataset_v06_model_ready.csv returns exactly 2 matches: MCONF-BTANRVKWQNVYAZ-298 and MCONF-FXHOOIRPVKKKFG-303.15 - i.e. precisely the two conflicts under adjudication. 2 of 56 (3.6%) UNRESOLVED conflicts are shipped as training labels. (2) ROOT CAUSE - NOT A COINCIDENCE. The 17 conflicted molecules are partitioned 2 model_ready / 14 excluded / 1 absent from v04. The 14 exclusions are blocked for UNRELATED reasons: PRESSURE_HETEROGENEOUS (13), PAIR_NOT_VALID (10), NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENT (2). NOT ONE exclusion row anywhere in the file carries a conflict-derived reason; the exception_class vocabulary is {NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENT, SYNTHETIC_PAIR_FROM_INDEPENDENT_MEDIAN, SOURCE_LAYER_MISMATCH_FALSE_NEGATIVE} and contains no CONFLICT class. The two leaking rows are simply the conflicted molecules that happened to have NO OTHER disqualifier. Exclusion is therefore incidental, not conflict-driven. (3) THE GATE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. All 74 model_ready rows carry flags='NONE' and blocking_reasons=NaN, including the two rows the conflict register labels UNRESOLVED. A downstream consumer reading only dataset_v06_model_ready.csv has no signal whatsoever that these labels are contested. (4) TWO INCOMPATIBLE WINDOW DEFINITIONS. build_source_conflict_register.py sets T_TOLERANCE_K=0.5 K and REL_EPS_TOLERANCE=2%, so a 'conflict' means same T within 0.5 K. build_dataset_v06.py sets BAND_LOW/BAND_HIGH = 293.15/303.15 K, a 10.0 K window. A row can therefore be conflict-free by construction (no two points within 0.5 K) while its aggregate pools observations spanning 10 K and stamps them with a single temperature. This is the mechanism that makes a 10 K pool masquerade as a 298.15 K datum for butan-2-ol. (5) THE DETECTOR IGNORES STATED UNCERTAINTY. The 2% flat tolerance is applied to point estimates only. For butan-2-ol a +/-10.8% measurement is flagged as conflicting with +/-0.36% measurements; an uncertainty-aware test (do the stated intervals overlap?) would not raise that conflict at all. The register consequently mixes real disagreements (DMAc: intervals disjoint) with precision artefacts (butan-2-ol: intervals nested), and the two cannot be told apart from the register alone. (6) LEDGER COVERAGE IS INCOMPLETE FOR BOTH SUBJECTS. For butan-2-ol, 18 pure raw rows reduce to 15 ledger rows; for DMAc, 22 reduce to 12. The conflict windows were computed on the reduced set. Omissions include the three DMAc 303.15 K points (37.499/37.515/37.552) that bear directly on the disputed value. (7) CONSEQUENCE FOR B05. Training on an UNRESOLVED label teaches the model a value that is, for DMAc, known to be a duplicate-counting artefact. The duplicate also inflates apparent sample size (n_contributing_measurements=3 for DMAc when 2 experiments exist), which is precisely the failure mode the project already recorded for the GVL conflict. The project's own bar is 4/4 PASS (see outputs/admission_v2/gvl_conflict_consensus.csv); two rows cannot be promoted on a 1-of-4 basis. RECOMMENDED FIX (ordering matters): (a) make build_dataset_v06.py read the conflict register and emit CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED into blocking_reasons so such rows can never be model_ready; (b) reconcile BAND_LOW/BAND_HIGH with T_TOLERANCE_K, or record the band span explicitly instead of a point temperature; (c) make the detector uncertainty-aware; (d) dedupe by evidence_group before any median; (e) close the raw-to-ledger coverage gap. Until (a) lands, no aggregate carrying an UNRESOLVED conflict may enter model-ready.
